span.label: The abstract reports the two abilities TOGETHER as no better than the comparison, and each ability SEPARATELY as better than the same comparison; the three statements do not compose and are not reconciled.
span.note: what this limits: citing this study for whether STAD cooperative learning outperforms problem-solving learning: the abstract's combined result says no better while both component results say better, and the paper does not state which reading holds

span.label: The whole population was used as the sample, so there is no sampling beyond the single class group studied.
span.note: what this limits: the generality of these results: the population is all 60 students of class VII at one school, and the analysis treats the data as coming from a saturated sample

span.label: THE ABSTRACT'S THIRD FINDING IS CONTRADICTED BY THE PAPER'S OWN MEANS. It states that problem-solving ability is better under STAD than under problem-solving learning; the reported means are 51.467 for STAD and 62.800 for problem-solving learning, so STAD is 11.3 points WORSE on that measure. The direction of the claim is the opposite of the direction of the data, and both are in this paper.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: A second impossible standard deviation: variance 145.640 with SD 62.609, where the square root is 12.068.
